parts.text:
14 A bicycle pedal is connected to a pivot by a metal bar, as shown.
force 60 N
pedal
bar
12 cm
20 cm
pivot
16 cm
The force on the pedal is 60 N downwards.
What is the moment of this force about the pivot?
A
7.2 N m
B
9.6 N m
C
12 N m
D
1200 N m

hints: Notice the $60 \text{ N}$ force acts vertically downwards on the pedal, so look for the horizontal distance from the pivot to its line of action in the diagram.
Recall moment $=$ force $\times$ perpendicular distance, so the $16 \text{ cm}$ side matters here, not the $12 \text{ cm}$ vertical side or the $20 \text{ cm}$ bar.
Convert the chosen distance from cm to m before multiplying by $60 \text{ N}$ to get the moment in $\text{N m}$.
walkthrough: Identify the force and pivot: $F = 60 \text{ N}$ downwards at the pedal, moment taken about the pivot at the bottom of the bar.
State the rule: moment $= F \times d$, where $d$ is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.

For a vertical force, the perpendicular distance is the horizontal separation. From the dashed triangle this is $16 \text{ cm}$, while $12 \text{ cm}$ is parallel to the force and $20 \text{ cm}$ is along the angled bar.
Convert to SI units: $d = 16 \text{ cm} = 0.16 \text{ m}$.
Calculate: moment $= 60 \times 0.16 = 9.6 \text{ N m}$ with a clockwise turning effect.

A.explanation: Uses the $12 \text{ cm}$ vertical separation: $60 \times 0.12 = 7.2 \text{ N m}$. This is parallel to the $60 \text{ N}$ force, not the perpendicular distance.

B.explanation: Uses the $16 \text{ cm}$ horizontal distance perpendicular to the vertical force: $60 \times 0.16 = 9.6 \text{ N m}$.

C.explanation: Uses the $20 \text{ cm}$ bar length: $60 \times 0.20 = 12 \text{ N m}$. The bar is at an angle, so its full length is not perpendicular to the force.

D.explanation: Multiplies $60 \text{ N}$ by $20 \text{ cm}$ without converting to metres to give $1200$. The moment must be in $\text{N m}$, not $\text{N cm}$.
